claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder is a cobalt-free high-entropy-alloy feedstock suitable for additive manufacturing.
An adaptive system can adjust laser power and scan speed in real time from in situ thermal feedback during L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser powers below 250 W constitute a typical practical processing range for L-PBF fabrication of this HEA.
Mechanical testing will be conducted under ambient laboratory conditions.
Adaptive machine-learning-guided laser scanning improves the mechanical integrity of L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi relative to fixed-parameter processing.
Real-time adjustment of laser parameters reduces melt-pool thermal gradients and produces more uniform melt-pool dynamics.
Reduced thermal gradients and more uniform melt-pool dynamics produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Adaptive processing produces a finer grain distribution in AlCrFeNiSi.
Adaptive processing minimizes segregation at AlCrFeNiSi grain boundaries.
Rapid thermal cycles and high thermal gradients cause compositional segregation and residual-stress buildup during L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
Machine learning trained on prior process data from similar HEAs can predict laser parameters that maintain a steady melt pool in AlCrFeNiSi.
Maintaining steady melt-pool conditions reduces defect formation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Adaptive processing will lower residual stresses relative to fixed-parameter L-PBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Adaptive processing will decrease microsegregation relative to fixed-parameter L-PBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Adaptive processing will decrease defect density relative to fixed-parameter L-PBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Adaptive processing will increase both tensile strength and ductility relative to fixed-parameter L-PBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional fixed-parameter additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi commonly produces notable segregation, high residual stress, and defects.
The hypothesis is restricted to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi processed by L-PBF within typical industrial parameter ranges.
